source: Let's make a grand theft auto type game. 3D, basic user avatar, basic movements using system control. Let's start with city generation and NPCs. NPCs should just walk around on the sidewalks for now. We'll build on top of this foundation

image_prompt.text: A central oversized city plaza sized to handle heavy avatar density without traffic jams
Sidewalks running along both sides of every street, sized for pedestrian foot traffic
Wide grid-aligned city streets, 30 studs two-way, meeting at right-angle intersections so vehicle meshes turn without clipping
Detailed street corners and small pocket parks built as backdrops for screenshots and roleplay scenes
A tall distinct downtown tower visible from across the city so players can navigate by sight

layout_placement.text: NPC pedestrians spawned along the sidewalks, walking in both directions

notes: Genre forced: an open-world crime city has no genre of its own. Roleplay & Avatar Sim's static settlement was the closest prebuilt-town shape.
No option covers NPC population or pedestrian pathing, so it is carried as free text in layout_placement.
The prompt scopes this to a foundation pass - city and pedestrians only - so no crime, mission, or vehicle-theft content was built.
path-road-vehicle was taken from the GTA reference rather than an explicit ask; drop it if the first pass is walking-only.

open_questions.ask: Should the city read as gritty and realistic, or bright and stylized?
How large should the first city be - a few blocks to test movement on, or a full district?
Once the city exists, what do players do in it - missions, free roam, jobs?

coverage_missing.ask: Should the city read as gritty and realistic, or bright and stylized?
How many city blocks should the first pass cover?
What is the loop in the city - crime missions, free roam, or jobs?

answers.ask: Should the city read as gritty and realistic, or bright and stylized?
answers.answer: Use a gritty, realistic urban city look to match the grand theft auto-style premise.

answers.ask: How large should the first city be - a few blocks to test movement on, or a full district?
answers.answer: Start with a few connected city blocks for a small, playable movement and NPC foundation.

answers.ask: Once the city exists, what do players do in it - missions, free roam, jobs?
answers.answer: Free roam for now; the prompt only calls for the city and walking NPC foundation, with gameplay added later.
